tasks.title: Digital study tools: access and responsibility
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: Your class has listened to a radio discussion about how universities should manage the use of digital study tools (such as AI tutors, online practice platforms and automated feedback systems). You have made the notes below.

promptBlocks.heading: Priorities for managing digital study tools
listItems: ensuring equal access for students with limited internet or devices
maintaining academic integrity when using AI tools

promptBlocks.heading: Some opinions expressed in the discussion:
paragraphs: If some students can't afford reliable internet, digital tools will widen the gap instead of closing it.
We can't just hand over student data to tech companies without clear safeguards.
AI tools make it too easy to cheat – we need clear rules about what's allowed.

promptBlocks.text: Write an essay for your tutor discussing two of the priorities in your notes. You should explain which priority you think is more important for universities to address, giving reasons in support of your answer. You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the discussion, but you should use your own words as far as possible.

tasks.title: Proposal for a digital study tools policy
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: Your university is developing a policy on digital study tools and has invited proposals from students. The policy should balance the convenience of these tools with the responsibility of using them ethically and sustainably.

Write a proposal for the university's academic policy committee. In your proposal, you should:

• recommend two specific guidelines for the ethical use of AI-powered study tools
• explain how these guidelines would benefit both students and the institution
• suggest how the university could monitor compliance and address violations

tasks.title: Email to programme coordinator
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.subject: Digital study tools pilot – your views
paragraphs: As you know, the university is planning a pilot programme that would give all first-year students free access to a suite of digital study tools, including an AI writing assistant and a personalised practice platform. Some staff have raised concerns that this might encourage over-reliance on technology and reduce students' independent learning skills.

I would like to hear your views on this initiative. Please write back explaining your position, analysing one potential drawback of the pilot, and proposing a way to address that drawback while still moving forward.

tasks.title: Review of a digital study tool
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: You see this announcement on an English-language student advice website.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted: Digital study tools
paragraphs: Have you used a digital study tool (e.g., an AI tutor, a flashcard app, or an online practice platform) to help with your coursework? We want to hear about your experience.

Write a review of the tool you used. Describe what it does and how easy it was to use. Evaluate how well it balanced convenience with helping you learn independently. Would you recommend it to other students? Why or why not?
The best reviews will be published on our website.
